questions.stem: Which subatomic particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons (positively charged) and neutrons (no charge). Electrons orbit the nucleus in shells outside it. The nucleus is very small compared to the overall atom but contains almost all of its mass.

questions.stem: A student writes 'CO' as the symbol for cobalt. Why is this incorrect?

options.text: Cobalt does not have a chemical symbol
CO represents carbon monoxide; cobalt is written as Co
The symbol for cobalt is Cb
Chemical symbols can only have one letter

questions.explanation: In chemical symbols, the first letter is always capitalised and the second letter (if present) is always lowercase. 'Co' is cobalt, while 'CO' represents the compound carbon monoxide (carbon and oxygen).
